paper_metadata.title: Accelerating Quantum Monte Carlo Calculations with Set-Equivariant Architectures and Transfer Learning

summary: This paper presents classical set-transformer models trained on variational QMC samples for a 1D long-range transverse-field Ising chain, achieving 3–4 orders of magnitude faster expectation-value evaluation than direct QMC post-processing. Reported results include phase classification on 50-spin systems, regression of ⟨m_z^2⟩ and ⟨m_z^4⟩, and transfer-learning prediction of the second Rényi entropy across 50, 100, and 150 spins, with an example speedup of about ×100 for N=50 and ×1800 for N=100.

experiments.description: Set-transformer classifier trained on QMC samples to detect magnetic phase (ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, paramagnetic) for a 1D long-range transverse-field Ising chain.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input is an array of spin configurations with values ±1; each sample is divided into fixed-sized tokens and padded/masked to allow variable sample counts.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Multiclass phase classification from QMC samples (ferromagnetic vs antiferromagnetic vs paramagnetic).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Attention masks for variable sample counts; nested binary classification used instead of direct ternary classifier.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_{ij} J_ij sigma^z_i sigma^z_j - h sum_i sigma^x_i with long-range couplings J_ij = J/eta for i=j and J/(eta |i-j|^alpha) otherwise.

problem_instance.description: Long-range transverse-field Ising chain phase classification over a grid of coupling ratios and decay exponents.

dataset_specification.description: Ground states generated by variational QMC for chains of 50 spins; alpha in [0,6] with step 0.4 and J/h in [-5,10] with step 0.375; training uses alpha in {0,3.2,6}.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Subsample aggregation augmentation: randomly choose a training example, draw a random subsample size c in [1,1024], subsample c configurations, and use the same label; applied to train/validation/test sets.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Trained for 500 epochs; evaluated on held-out validation/test sets across the parameter grid.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Adam optimizer for classifier training; QMC/NetKet used to generate labels
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: QMC ground-state generation; data augmentation by random subsampling; padding and attention masks.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Softmax output; nested binary classification to map to three phases.
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 500 epochs; training duration not otherwise quantified for classifier

speedup_claims.baseline_method: direct expectation-value evaluation from QMC samples
speedup_claims.conditions: for calculating expectation values with the set-transformer architecture
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as a general claim in the introduction; later text gives specific examples of roughly 100x for N=50 and 1800x for N=100.

experiments.description: Set-transformer regressor trained with transfer learning to predict the second Renyi entanglement entropy across system sizes 50, 100, and 150 spins.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Training on 50-spin system followed by retraining heads on 100- and 150-spin systems; exact stopping criterion not specified

hyperparameters.transfer_learning_freeze_strategy: freeze main architectural block; retrain final heads

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input is a set of sampled spin configurations; for transfer learning, input uses ternary values {0,1,2} where 2 denotes missing spins.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Regression of the second Renyi entanglement entropy from QMC samples.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Permutation invariance; ternary input embedding to accommodate different system sizes; averaging labels over five QMC realizations per parameter point.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_{ij} J_ij sigma^z_i sigma^z_j - h sum_i sigma^x_i.

problem_instance.description: Entanglement-entropy regression near the ferromagnetic-paramagnetic transition for long-range Ising chains.

dataset_specification.description: Reference ground states generated for alpha in {1.66,1.7,2.5,6} and chain lengths 50, 100, 150; training uses alpha in {1.66,6}.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: For each {J/h, alpha} pair, five QMC runs are performed and labeled with the mean S2; transfer learning uses ternary input with missing-spin token 2.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Predictions compared against QMC and literature; finite-size scaling and log-volume-law fits performed.

implementation_details.classical_solver: SGD; QMC/NetKet for data generation; Savitzky-Golay filter and finite-size scaling analysis
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Five QMC realizations per parameter point averaged into a single label; ternary encoding for missing spins; transfer learning by freezing the main block and retraining heads.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Savitzky-Golay smoothing; linear regression for log-volume-law; finite-size scaling collapse.
implementation_details.total_execution_time: Initial training about 15 minutes; each subsequent transfer-learning stage about 11 minutes (reported for the overall workflow).
